thread:
maya: Heads-up — prototype for an "adaptive cost slab" card landed in the console PR: https://git.redwood/infra/console/pulls/582. Looking for quick feedback on attribution text and sampling implications.

sam: saw the PR, nice! quick q: how does this change attribution when requests are routed across variants? e.g., modelA -> modelA-quant -> fallback?

liam: short answer: we currently split prefetch credits evenly across routes that touched the prefetched KV, but the new adapter tries to weight by last-touch probability. still sketchy.

noor: from UX: users expect the savings to look deterministic per-route. changing to probabilistic weights might confuse them — can we show a confidence band or sample rate? :thinking_face:

maya: good call. plan was to expose a small badge: "sampled" with hover → sample rate & confidence interval. default sample rate = 1% for historical views.

sam: 1% seems low for small tenants — their APIs will be noisy. can we make it tenant-adaptive? e.g., auto-increase sampling for low-traffic tenants.

liam: yes, we can. data pipeline supports dynamic sample rate per tenant window. cost of extra sampling is small vs value. implementation detail: we need to propagate a sampling tag through router metadata so the chargeback agg can reweight.

jenna: ops note: propagate tags carefully, we hit cardinality explosions before when we attached route+variant+traceid. pls ensure tags are limited to stable keys: tenant_id, route_id, sample_bucket.

ops-bot: deploy queued: console/feature/adaptive-slab @staging on host infra-console-stg-3 (rollout will start in 2m). :rocket:

noor: quick micro-UX thought: show "estimated cache-savings" vs "attributed cache-savings" and a tooltip that explains heuristics. keeps transparency without full math.

sam: +1. also add a toggle in the rollout that lets us switch from last-touch weighting to even-split for A/B testing. need this to verify regressions.

maya: can do — add a server flag and a console toggle. rollout plan: 10% tenants -> 50% -> 100% over 48h with canary guard based on net-cost-delta and error-rate.

liam: for instrumentation, I'll emit a metric: cost_attribution_method{tenant,method=last_touch|even_split, sample_rate}. we can wire that to the cost-slo alert.

jenna: set alert if median per-tenant delta > 15% for 30m or 95p latency regresses. we should be able to rollback quickly.

noor: design will draft the badge copy + tooltip today. attaching mock in the PR. pls review: https://figma.redwood/console/adaptive-cost-card

sam: small nit in PR: console is showing token delta rounded to integer tokens — for small savings we lose signal. please show two decimal places for token-equivalent and microcost.

maya: agreed, liam do you have the microcost conversion?

liam: using dynamic sku rate from billing service, conversion emitted as usd_per_token metric. I'll add that field to the API response.

ops-bot: staged deploy started: console/feature/adaptive-slab @staging (build 582.1). monitor: https://dash.redwood/s/redeploys/582.1

maya: thanks all. action items: liam add sample_rate + usd_per_token fields; sam add even_split toggle + rounding change; noor finish tooltip; jenna add alert rules; i'll update rollout doc.

sam: I'll also add an opt-out endpoint for tenants that want deterministic legacy attribution. quick and dirty: POST /admin/tenants/:id/feature-flags {"adaptive_slab": false}.

liam: caution: opt-out must also stop emitting sample tags for that tenant, otherwise aggregator still applies heuristics. will implement.

jenna: once staging looks good, do a 10% prod push with 1-hour monitoring window. call in #eng-oncall if anything spikes. :eyes:

maya: perfect. ping me in thread when staging pass. thanks!
